events.title: BCPL reference manual published
events.summary: Martin Richards published the BCPL reference manual as MIT Project MAC Memorandum M-352.
events.about: BCPL (Basic Combined Programming Language) was a simple systems language for writing compilers and OS code — stripped-down CPL without heavy type rules. Ken Thompson read this manual at Bell Labs and used BCPL's ideas to build B, then C. BCPL's `$` operator survives today as C's indirection syntax lineage.

narrative.whyChosen: BCPL is the direct ancestor of B and therefore C — the missing link between ALGOL and Unix systems programming.
narrative.whyImportant: Richards showed a small, compile-friendly language could target many machines — a template Thompson and Ritchie followed.
narrative.problemSolved: Full CPL was too complex to compile efficiently; systems programmers needed a lean language for tools and compilers.
